verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This is the largest cited-input set in the series and it is clean: 93 path/digest pairs verified by recursive walk, zero mismatches, zero missing files, with recordedInputs.HEAD equal to the top-level head and live HEAD. The two new measurements hold on inspection rather than assertion — all twelve doctor FC INPUT corpora are cited, all twelve digests match, and each is independently ACCEPT 0/0 with CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING and no Codex file, mapping one-to-one onto the twelve classes OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING still names; and the join catalog's thirteen FC-JOIN ids are == equal to live actor-join v8's, matching OBL-JOIN-FX-AUTHORING's thirteen. Both new obligations are leftoverDesign false in specifiedNotLeftover and each expressly declines to close its authoring counterpart, so the eight obligations the dispatch protects remain exactly the leftover set. Identity is consistent across the whole chain, v1/1 through v6/6, with exactly one version self-reference sentence and it is the accurate one. I went behind the byte-invention claim to FC-RO, the pre-image and post-image class most at risk, and found its corpus carries those three byte-sets as NOT-AUTHORED with explicit denials. The one thing that looked wrong — lands citing CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1, my finding against a different family — is scoped correctly to predecessor role sentences within this artifact, and is justified: frozen v5's predecessorV3 role does read 'This v4 does not reuse the v3 version number' in a v5 artifact, a defect my own v5 review passed as ACCEPT 0/0 and missed. v6 caught it, fixed it, and named the finding rather than repairing it silently.
